abstract: Dirac delta functions enter classical and statistical mechanics most prominently as constraint distributions, for example in microcanonical measures \rho_E(z)\propto \delta(H(z)-E) and in phase-space integrals restricted to a constraint surface. In the delta/projection program of Modal Triplet Theory (MTT), such deltas are not treated as primitive objects. They are re-read as singular limits of finite admissibility shells: finite-thickness neighborhoods around constraint surfaces that become exact only when the allowed tolerance is sent to zero. This paper develops the classical/statistical-mechanical member of that program. We prove a coarea-based shell theorem: for a regular value E of a smooth Hamiltonian H:M\to\mathbb R, normalized approximate identities \eta_\varepsilon(H(z)-E) converge distributionally to the surface delta \delta(H-E), with the standard coarea measure d\Sigma/\left\lvert \nabla H \right\rvert. We then formulate finite-thickness microcanonical shells, show their convergence to the sharp microcanonical measure, and interpret the result in MTT language: \delta(H-E) is the zero-thickness limit of an admissibility shell around a bookkeeping constraint. The paper also distinguishes three layers often conflated in formal notation: exact constraint surfaces, finite experimental/thermodynamic tolerance shells, and singular delta notation. The result is a concrete extension of the delta/projection program from QFT and measurement to classical and statistical mechanics.
title: Classical Constraint Deltas and Microcanonical Shells Admissibility-Shell Limits in Modal Triplet Theory
